(Photo by Ed Zurga/Getty Images) | Getty Images UCF and chaotic, seemingly inexplicable finishes have become quite the pairing this season. Two weeks after knocking off BYU in perhaps the wildest ending of the college football season , the Knights found themselves in another crunch time thriller Saturday, this time on the road at Kansas. For most of the contest, UCF appeared on track to secure its first comfortable victory in Big 12 play. The Knights built a 26-7 lead by the 9:52 mark of the third quarter, seemingly having solved the Jayhawks on both sides of the ball. But their next two possessions went nowhere, producing consecutive three-and-outs that combined for -6 yards. That sudden offensive futility left the door ajar for a Kansas comeback, and the Jayhawks capitalized with two-straight touchdown drives and a field goal to trim the deficit to 26-24. Then, following a spectacular punt by Atticus Bertrams, Kansas regained possession at its own 5-yard line with 2:27 remaining, needing just a field goal to complete the program’s largest comeback since 2010. Somehow, the Jayhawks crammed 11 plays and 95 yards into 81 seconds, capping the clutch drive with a Dylan Edwards touchdown run with 1:06 remaining, catapulting Kansas ahead 32-26. But the scoring drive was so quick that it granted UCF 66 seconds of opportunity while armed with two timeouts. The drive did not start in promising fashion as the Knights opened the drive with several misfires. But quarterback Alonza Barnett III — making his first start since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 2 — caught fire, jumpstarting the offense with a 20-yard completion to Tyren Hornes on 3rd-and-10. Barnett lofted a pass toward the back of the end zone, where Derry made a juggling grab while falling backward. The official initially threw his hands up to signal touchdown, but the replay review showed Derry had not secured possession before landing out of bounds. The call was overturned, leaving UCF eight seconds to work with. The next attempt didn’t produce a touchdown, but it still benefited the Knights. top.title: On the future of the NBA in Mexico, from the Global Games to a franchise
top.description: MEXICO CITY: No city outside the United States or Canada has hosted more regular season NBA games than Mexico City. So it should come as no surprise that the annual tilts held in the Mexican capital are the frequent backdrop for rumbles about the league setting up shop on a more permanent basis in the largest metropolis on the continent. In recent years, however, the league making a return to the Pacific Northwest to put a new team back in Seattle, Washington along with a new team in Las Vegas, Nevada seemed a fait accompli, and with it, hope for an NBA team in the city faded. But before the start of the 2026 season, it was announced at an NBA Board of Governor's meeting that Mexico City was back in the mix with a potential ownership group and arena district lined up. Still, the Mexico City Game has been and will likely remain the gem in the crown of the league that is their Global Games series, a yearly accomplishment on its own signifying the nascent talent and fandom of Latin America now percolating into the league's ranks. To learn more, the Rookie Wire caught up with NBA Latin America and Canada Head of Operations Raul Zarraga ahead of the 2026 Mexico City Game between the Denver Nuggets and Indiana Pacers . From the state of the Association in Mexico, and what the future of Mexico City Games and NBA expansion in the region might look like, our conversation covered the gamut and then some. This interview has been lightly edited for the purposes of clarity and brevity. Rookie Wire: What it is you do with regard to the Mexico City games? Raul Zarraga : Of course. The Global Game – it's a great opportunity for us. You have this life experience for fans and partners and everyone in the community, and all the people enjoying the game. Keep in mind that less than one percent of people around the world have the opportunity to be in-person for a regular season NBA game. And that's why it's very important for us to give a piece of that action to all the fans in Mexico. I wish we could have many more games available for fans. But we are very happy with the experience so far. It's sold out in a couple of days. The two amazing teams, we're really looking forward to (having them) here: the Pacers and the Nuggets. The Pacers for the first time, the Nuggets the second, and it's a whole celebration together, a unique way to mix two very important components: entertainment and the culture. Something that the fans are really looking for, regardless if they are core, casual, (or) curious fans of our 30 million fans (in Latin America), this is a great opportunity to enjoy the NBA. And we have other assets at the Capitanes (Mexico City's G League team) as well for live experiences. So we have this regular season (game), and then we tip off the season for Capitanes for 21 games of regular season happening here. top.title: Best division ever? How NFC North is on pace to make history in 2026
top.description: Best division ever? How NFC North is on pace to make history in 2026 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Bears found a way to win on Sunday night, overcoming five turnovers to defeat the Buccaneers 27-24, but they certainly aren't alone in the NFC North. The Packers and Lions both continued their winning ways on Sunday, and, until Monday at least, none of those three teams can say they only one loss like the Vikings do. All four NFC North teams will enter Week 10 in the playoff picture. While head-to-head matchups might hurt the division's chances of getting every team into the playoffs, it's becoming clear these four teams are in a class of their own as a group. Here's a look at how the NFC North could be headed for uncharted territory. MORE: Which NFL trade candidates boosted - or hurt - their stocks in Week 9? NFC North combined record The NFC North is now 25-8 (.757) through nearly nine weeks, with five of those eight losses simply coming against one another. NFC North teams are 20-3 in non-divisional games. Here are the standings after Sunday night, with the Vikings still to play on Monday: Team Record Pct. Vikings 6-1 .857 Bears 7-2 .778 Lions 6-2 .750 Packers 6-3 .667 Every team in the division is at least three games over .500, meaning the Packers are in last place at 6-3. In the NFC North, for comparison, the 3-5 Panthers lead the division. The Bears have had a hard time gaining ground during the four-game win streak because of all of the success around them, but a Vikings loss to the Bills on Monday night would rocket Chicago into first place. MORE: 4 quarterbacks who boosted their early MVP cases in Week 9 Best division in NFL history When it comes to divisions, there are two distinct periods in the NFL: pre-2002, when divisions were larger than four teams, and 2002-present, when all divisions have been comprised of four teams. The overall records within divisions were more even before 2002 because more teams were in each. Since 2002, the best record for a division belongs to the 2024 NFC North, which saw teams go a combined 45-23 (.662) as the Lions went 15-2, Vikings went 14-3, Packers went 11-6 and Bears went 7-10. Two years earlier, in the NFC East went a combined 43-23-2, sending three teams to the playoffs. So far, the NFC North is on track to break its own record in 2026. At 25-8 (.757), every team is at least three games above .500 and their combined record would have to be 20-15 the rest of the way to match the 2024 mark. There are still seven divisional games on the docket in the NFC North, so the division will have at least 15 losses. If these four teams can keep it to only eight additional losses, the division will tie its own record from 2002. top.title: Mitch Albom: Lions won't have many easy wins. But does it matter?
top.description: Dan Campbell knew what this was by halftime. He barked it into the CBS cameras. “We gotta calm down … and then we GOTTA GO! We can’t be messing around!” Exactly. When playing a team that is 1-6, a good team often finds itself inexplicably fumbling and bumbling. It’s like when you can’t get that first piece of plastic to peel off the box. You start normal, then you try your fingernails, then you get frustrated, and you wind up screaming to yourself, “Why is this so damn hard?” That was the Detroit Lions for much of Sunday’s game in Miami against the low-win but high-effort Dolphins . Detroit’s first drive used up nearly seven minutes but ended with a sack of Jared Goff on third-and-goal. A field goal had to suffice. Their second drive ended in an interception, when Goff was pressured and a defender hit his arm as he tried to pass. Their third drive ended with a punt. Their fourth drive, after starting with great field position, fizzled when Jahmyr Gibbs was yanked down twice in a row for thre- yard losses and Goff was pressured into a scramble. Another field goal. The NFL’s highest-flying offense was hovering very close to the ground. Fortunately, Miami couldn’t take advantage. They punted twice, notched a field goal, and wasted an 11-play drive with a doink off the uprights by their kicker, Zane Gonzalez. Halftime ended at Lions 6, Miami 3. Which is what led Campbell to his “we can’t be messing around” critique, which I’m sure he delivered in the locker room with a fervor that would have scared the average TV viewer. And eventually, they did stop messing around. And they finally brought home a 19-9 win that may have certain critics attacking them for, well, not being able to get the plastic off a box faster than that. They’d be wrong. Join us live on YouTube after every Lions game. ] Settling in Remember, this is a team coming off an emotional injury to one of their most beloved and important players, linebacker Jack Campbell. It swirled around practice all week. When one football player sees another football player face down and not moving, it stays with them − believe me. Dealing with Campbell’s health uncertainly, then getting a positive message from him midweek, then having to focus on an opponent that should be easy to beat ... well, all that is a perfect recipe for the old trap game, where you go home shaking your head saying, “How did we lose to them ?” That didn’t happen Sunday against the Dolphins, and the Lions first deserve credit for that. Four plays into the second half, safety Chuck Clark snagged a Malik Willis pass and turned into a running back, cutting angles and using blocks. He returned the ball 34 yards to the Miami 26. top.title: Boston Celtics rally to stomp Milwaukee Bucks, 117-97, and improve to 8-2
top.description: Effort is difficult to quantify in the NBA. However, there are a few areas of the game that can occasionally reveal its presence. For an example of this phenomenon during the Boston Celtics' 117-97 win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Sunday night, look no further than the final offensive rebound totals. The C's corralled a whopping 20 offensive boards at Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee while the Bucks only grabbed 9. Such a significant disparity suggests that the Celtics, who trailed 20-6 about halfway through the first quarter, stepped up their effort when things didn't immediately go their way. In fact, 4 of Boston's 6 offensive rebounds in the first frame occurred after it went down double digits. Meanwhile, Milwaukee had 0 offensive rebounds in that same span, and just 1 in the entire first quarter. Because the Celtics dominated the glass, they ended up with 16 more field goal attempts than the Bucks. From there, it's a math game, as Boston converted on 45 of its 95 shots (47.4 percent from the field) while Milwaukee hit 35 of its 79 shots (44.3 percent from the field). As for the rest of the margins, the Celtics garnered 12 steals — another effort-related stat — to the Bucks' 5 and prevailed in the points in the paint battle, 44-28. All of these numbers added up to the Celtics' third straight win and the Bucks' sixth straight loss. top.description: (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) | Getty Images Never say never on Woltemade to Bayern (Sport Bild’s Christian Falk) Will Bayern Munich eventually throw Nick Woltemade a life preserver to help save his career? Sport Bild’s Christian Falk will not fully rule it out—it just will not happen any time soon: “I can say it’s not true that Bayern are concretely interested in Nick Woltemade at the moment. I won’t say that he’s categorically not an idea for the future. However, he has to perform. He has scored a few goals for Juventus, but most of these are penalties. He’s not in the starting XI in the league and it’s the same problem in the national team. Ultimately, we have to see more of the performances he was putting in during his peak at VfB Stuttgart. At the moment, he looks a shadow of the player we all saw and enjoyed in the Bundesliga. Of course, we have to emphasize that he’s young (24), he has talent and can play. nigeria.description: By Jide Ajani There is perhaps no greater threat to electoral integrity than an unreliable Voters’ Register. Before the first ballot is cast or the first result announced, the credibility of an election is already being determined by the document that establishes who is entitled to vote. Read Also: * Explainer: Who won 2023 presidential 2023 in Kaduna, Katsina – the 161,829 votes difference * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal The Voters’ Register is the foundation of the electoral process. It defines the electorate, determines the numerical strength of constituencies and provides the basis for accreditation and voting. It is, fundamentally, the official record of a people’s democratic membership. Yet, in Nigeria, its credibility remains a persistent source of anxiety. The historical paradox: have we really progressed? Nigeria has travelled a considerable distance from the largely manual registration arrangements of the 1950s to biometric registration, electronic databases and the deployment of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). The 1959 general election, conducted under the Electoral Commission of Nigeria (ECN), had approximately nine million registered voters. Subsequent elections in 1964/65, 1979, 1983 and 1993 exposed different administrative and political challenges associated with voter registration. 4th Republic The Fourth Republic introduced more sophisticated systems, including permanent voter cards, biometric identification and mechanisms for detecting duplicate registrations. Yet technological advancement has not necessarily translated into greater electoral credibility. A bigger register is not automatically a better register. A digital register is not necessarily reliable, and biometric technology is not beyond manipulation. Consider the fluctuations in registration figures: 73.5 million in 2011, 67.4 million in 2015 and approximately 84 million in 2019. Such changes do not establish manipulation, since legitimate deletions and corrections occur The real test is fidelity: whether the names represent living, eligible citizens entitled to vote, or whether they are mere AI-generated entities. INEC and the collapse of public confidence An electoral commission’s credibility rests not merely on constitutional independence but on demonstrable impartiality, competence and transparency. Constitutional independence in itself does not guarantee operational independence when the personnel saddled with responsibilities decide to go rogue on the system. When public confidence in INEC declines, virtually every administrative decision becomes vulnerable to suspicion, from voter registration and PVC distribution to accreditation and results management. nigeria.title: Zuba fruit market traders decry poor access road
nigeria.description: Some traders at Zuba Fruit Market, Federal Capital Territory (FCT), have decried the poor access road, saying it disrupts business activities, discourages customers and increases transportation costs. They spoke in separate interviews with the News Agency of Nigeria on Wednesday in Abuja. They said the road, which had deteriorated over time, becomes almost impassable during the rainy season due to deep potholes, muddy sections and poor drainage. According to them, the poor condition of the road discourages customers from visiting the market and causes delays in transporting fresh fruits and vegetables. A fruit wholesaler, Mr Mohammed Usman, said many commercial vehicles avoided the road because of its poor state, forcing traders to pay higher transport fares. “The bad road has affected our business seriously. Many transporters charge extra because they fear damage to their vehicles. “Some customers also turn back when they see the condition of the road, while others prefer buying from markets with easier access,” he said. Another trader, Mr Augustine Igwe, said vehicles conveying fruits from farms frequently developed mechanical faults due to the poor condition of the road. One of the bad roads in Zuba “We spend more money repairing our vehicles and paying higher transport fares. These costs eventually increase the prices of fruits. “Sometimes, vehicles carrying fruits get stuck, leading to delays and spoilage of some produce. The extra cost is eventually passed on to buyers,” he said. A buyer, Mrs Esther Okoli, described the road as a major challenge, especially for elderly people and parents visiting the market with children. “The road is in a terrible state. Many customers complain before coming here, while transporters charge us more because of the bad road. “Whenever it rains, the road becomes almost impassable because of stagnant water and deep potholes. Carrying goods through such conditions is stressful,” she said. Another buyer, Mr Emmanuel Johnson, said the poor condition of the road increased the cost and difficulty of moving goods from the market. “I shop here for affordable prices, but the poor road discourages buyers. Commercial vehicles often avoid the market, forcing us to carry purchases over long distances. ”A commercial driver, Mr Abdullahi Ibrahim, said frequent use of the road increased vehicle maintenance costs due to damaged tyres and suspension systems. He appealed to the FCT Administration to prioritise the rehabilitation of the access road to improve transportation and support businesses operating in the market. NAN reports that Zuba Fruit Market supplies fruits and vegetables daily, serving thousands of consumers within the FCT and neighbouring communities. The traders and buyers expressed optimism that prompt government intervention would improve access to the market, reduce transportation costs and enhance economic activities in the area.(NAN)

nigeria.title: Sultan directs Muslims to sight Jumada Assaniya moon Monday
nigeria.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO – The Sultanate Council of Sokoto has called on Muslims across Nigeria to search for the new crescent moon of Jumada Assaniya 1448AH on Monday, November 9, 2026. The directive was contained in a statement dated November 8, 2026, signed by Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu and made available to journalists on Sunday. According to the statement, the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council identified Monday as the 29th day of Jumada al-Ula 1448AH and the appropriate date for the nationwide moon-sighting exercise. The council urged Muslims across the country to actively participate in the exercise by looking out for the new crescent moon after sunset on Monday. It specifically requested anyone who sights the crescent to promptly report the observation to the nearest District or Village Head for onward transmission to His Eminence, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, CFR, mni, the Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA). The council stressed the importance of timely and credible reports of confirmed sightings to enable the Sultan to make the appropriate religious announcement on the commencement of the new Islamic month. It noted that the Sultan remains the recognised authority responsible for communicating the outcome of the moon-sighting exercise to Muslims across the country. The announcement underscores the role of the Sultanate Council in coordinating Islamic religious affairs and guiding the Muslim Ummah on matters concerning the Islamic lunar calendar. In a prayer, Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu, Waziri and Chairman of the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council, asked Allah (SWT) to grant Muslims the guidance and strength to discharge the religious responsibility successfully. The council also prayed for divine assistance and acceptance of the exercise, urging Muslims to approach the assignment with sincerity, vigilance and a strong sense of religious commitment. nigeria.title: Fermin brace earns Liga leaders Barcelona 2-1 win at Atletico
nigeria.description: Fermin Lopez struck twice to help Barcelona come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 and move three points clear at the top of La Liga. The Spanish champions lead second place Real Madrid, who beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday, with Atletico third, now five points behind. Giuliano Simeone fired Atletico ahead in a high-octane start, before Lopez pulled Barca level shortly before the interval at the Metropolitano stadium. The 23-year-old Spain international netted the winner after 66 minutes when Lamine Yamal slipped him in. The match started at a fast pace and both teams hit the woodwork in the opening stages. Alvarez, who tried and failed to force a move from Atletico to Barca in the summer, rounded goalkeeper Joan Garcia but could not finish off the chance as the defence blocked his route to goal. From the resulting corner Atletico defender Marc Pubill headed against the crossbar with Garcia beaten. At the other end Pedri crashed a strike against the woodwork after being fed by Barca’s teenage star Lamine Yamal. Atletico took the lead in the 10th minute, slicing Barca’s defence open. Alvarez crossed for Giuliano Simeone to turn home from close range. The game settled down after that pulsating start, although Alvarez came close to scoring Atletico’s second. The Argentine international’s shot was fumbled by Garcia, but the goalkeeper was able to collect the ball quickly afterwards. Yamal blasted into the side-netting from a tight angle with Barcelona not able to click into their top gears. Despite their struggles they went in level at the break, with a goal out of nowhere. Lopez’s path to the box was blocked but the ball bounced loose to the midfielder and he quickly smashed a strike past Jan Oblak. Early in the second half Alvarez lobbed over the crossbar when running in on goal. The forward came to rue the miss when Barcelona took the lead. Yamal played a clever pass through Atletico’s defence and Lopez kept his cool to beat Oblak. It was his seventh league goal in 11 top flight appearances this season. Barcelona kept Atletico at bay well in the final stages to take three points home from the capital before the international break. Earlier on fourth-place Real Betis earned a 2-0 win at Elche, while Real Sociedad, fifth, defeated Rayo Vallecano 1-0. nigeria.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos APC Candidate Hamzat Promises 4,000 CNG Buses, 77 Electric Ferries
nigeria.description: The Lagos State governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Obafemi Hamzat, has promised to deploy 4,000 compressed natural gas (CNG) buses to move one million passengers daily as part of plans to ease transportation challenges in the state. Hamzat, the incumbent Deputy Governor, also disclosed plans to expand water transportation with 77 electric ferries and improve connectivity between different parts of Lagos through an integrated transport system. ﻿ He made the promises on Sunday during the Lagos governorship debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, The Cable, and Vanguard Newspaper. Explaining his transportation plans, Hamzat said the objective was to reduce commuting time and give residents more opportunities to rest and spend time with their families. “The plan is to give back time to the citizens to plan, to rest, to spend with their family. There’s nowhere in Africa that the private sector has funded a rail. “Since BRT started, it has done 77 million journeys; that is with 1,000 buses. My plan says we will push it to 4,000 buses; the idea is to move one million people a day with 4,000 CNG buses, meaning up to 5,000, create BRt lane from Marina to Epe, from Marina to Badagry and so on and so forth,” he said. “Today, over four million people have the Cowry card. What does that mean? It means you can use ferry, you can use rail, and you can use BRT buses — one payment — so that we can deal with how to subsidise it. On healthcare, the APC candidate promised to expand access to medical services by increasing the number of primary healthcare centres providing round-the-clock services. Hamzat said that out of the over 300 primary healthcare centres, the government planned to increase its flagship PHCs from 87 to 150, with the facilities operating 24 hours a day. He also disclosed that the state government was building more hospitals to improve healthcare access for residents. nigeria.title: Seven killed, over 100 injured in Egypt train collision
nigeria.description: At least seven people have been killed and more than 100 injured after two trains collided near Giza, Egypt, causing several carriages to derail and plunge down an embankment. The country’s railway authority said the trains, travelling south from Giza and Cairo, collided in the area between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat. Egypt’s President, Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, said he had directed relevant authorities to investigate the circumstances surrounding the accident and ensure that anyone found negligent was held accountable. The public prosecutor’s office warned that the death toll could rise as rescue and recovery operations continued. The government said hospitals in the affected area had been placed on heightened alert to handle the large number of casualties. Health Minister, Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, said victims were receiving treatment for various injuries, including broken bones and head injuries. The Egyptian Red Crescent also deployed personnel to provide emergency assistance and psychological support to victims and their families at the scene. The ministry confirmed that the driver of one of the trains was among those killed in the collision. According to reports, the first train was travelling from Giza to Fayoum when it crashed into the rear of another train heading from Cairo to Aswan, which was stationary on the tracks. Photographs from the scene showed several overturned carriages, with emergency responders and members of the public searching through the wreckage for survivors. Train services between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended as cranes were deployed to remove the damaged trains. The railway authority had yet to announce when services would resume. The crash occurred close to the location of Egypt’s deadliest railway disaster, which happened in February 2002 when a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor, killing more than 370 people officially, although some estimates put the death toll higher. Two other train accidents in the area in 2009 also claimed dozens of lives. The latest disaster sparked calls on Sunday for Egypt’s transport minister to resign over the recurring railway accidents. Meanwhile, foreign governments and diplomatic representatives expressed condolences and solidarity with Egypt over the tragedy. Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed solidarity with Egypt and wished the injured a speedy recovery. Turkey’s Ambassador to Egypt also conveyed his condolences on X to the victims, their families and the Egyptian people. nigeria.title: No Political Will To Deal With Agberos In Lagos, Says NDC’s Funsho Doherty
nigeria.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Lagos State, Funsho Doherty, has blamed the persistence of the agbero system in the state on a lack of political will by successive administrations to reform the transport sector. Agberos are transport touts who collect money from commercial bus drivers and other transport operators at motor parks, bus stops and along roads, often claiming to represent transport unions or park authorities. Speaking during the Lagos Governorship Debate on Sunday, Doherty said powerful interests within the existing transport system had made it difficult for successive governments to tackle the activities of the operators. The debate was organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, a coalition of five media organisations: Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard Newspapers. “Many of us understand this notion of the agbero system that people talk about. There is no political will to deal with that problem,” Doherty said. He argued that meaningful reform of public transportation would require a government that was accountable to residents rather than interests benefiting from the existing arrangement. “We will modernise the transportation system because we will be elected by the people, not by an agbero network,” he said. nigeria.title: Idris inaugurates APC 2027 Campaign Council in Kebbi
nigeria.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi Kebbi State Governor, Dr Nasir Idris, has inaugurated the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 Campaign Council, charging members to work towards securing victory for all party candidates in the forthcoming general elections. The governor inaugurated the council on Sunday at the Presidential Lodge, Birnin Kebbi, urging members to demonstrate commitment, dedication and determination in discharging their responsibilities. He described Kebbi as an APC stronghold and called on party stakeholders to return to their respective communities to mobilise support for the party’s candidates across all elective positions. Idris announced former Kebbi State Governor and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Turkey, Ambassador Saidu Usman Nasamu Dakingari, as chairman of the campaign council. “I have the honour and privilege of inaugurating this campaign council for the 2027 General Elections, which will be headed by the former Governor of Kebbi State and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Turkey, His Excellency, Ambassador Saidu Usman Nasamu Dakingari. I wish all members the very best of luck,” the governor said. Speaking at the event, the APC State Chairman, Alhaji Abubakar Kana-Zuru, commended Idris for his support for the party and commitment to the successful inauguration of the campaign council. He urged members to remain dedicated to campaign activities, work collectively and ensure the party’s success in the forthcoming elections. In his response, Dakingari thanked the governor for the confidence reposed in him and other members of the council. He assured the governor that the committee would work diligently and collectively to achieve the party’s objectives. “On behalf of all members of the committee, I assure you that we are fully committed to delivering on this assignment. We will work hard and put in our best to ensure the success of the APC in the 2027 General Elections,” he said. nigeria.title: Police arrest six suspected phone thieves at Makinde’s Bauchi rally
nigeria.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested six suspected phone thieves accused of stealing mobile phones from participants at the presidential campaign flag-off of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM) candidate, Governor Seyi Makinde, in the state. The suspects were arrested by operatives of the Police Violent Crimes Response Unit (VCRU), deployed to provide security at the campaign venue, following the detection of their suspicious movements during the event. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Nafiu Habib, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying exhibits were recovered from four of the suspects, while two others were identified by a victim as allegedly responsible for stealing his phone. The suspects were identified as Muhammad Rabiu, 20; Ibrahim Abubakar, 25; Hamza Usman, 18; Abba Bala, 20; Auwal Muhammad, 23; and Inusa Adamu, 20. Items recovered from them included an itel torchlight phone, an OPPO Android phone, an Infinix Smart 20 phone and a 20,000mAh power bank. The police spokesman said a Samsung Fold 4 allegedly stolen during the event had yet to be recovered, adding that efforts were being intensified to retrieve the device and other missing valuables. He said investigation was ongoing and that the suspects would be charged to court upon its conclusion. The Commissioner of Police, Sani-Omolori Aliyu, commended the operatives for their vigilance and prompt action, which led to the arrests and recovery of some stolen items. He warned criminal elements against exploiting public gatherings and political events to perpetrate crime, stressing that the command would not relent in its efforts to rid the state of criminal activities. The commissioner also urged members of the public attending political rallies and other public events to remain vigilant, safeguard their valuables and promptly report suspicious movements to security operatives. He called for continued public cooperation through the provision of timely and credible information to assist the command in preventing and controlling crime. nigeria.title: Police rescue five kidnap victims, arrest three suspects in Kebbi
nigeria.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has rescued five kidnapped victims and arrested three suspects following a coordinated security operation in Dakingari, Suru Local Government Area of the state. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman Kebbi, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the operation followed credible intelligence that armed men had invaded Dolen Kwandage Village and abducted three residents. The victims were identified as Samaila Abubakar, 35; Dayyaba Muhammadu, 32; and Balki Hakimi, 31. According to the statement, police operatives, working in collaboration with local vigilantes, swiftly mobilised to the area and pursued the assailants. The police said the superior firepower of the security team forced the kidnappers to abandon their captives, leading to the rescue of the three newly abducted residents and two other women who had earlier been held in captivity. The two women were identified as Moe Muddaha, 50, and Hadiza Bello, 30, both from Yarma Village in Suru LGA. All five victims were rescued unhurt and taken to the General Hospital, Dakingari, for medical examination before being reunited with their families. The operation also led to the arrest of three suspects identified as Umaru Janyo, 49, and Bube Kwaire, 28, both from Bendu Village, and Muhammadu Gyade, 22, of Tindifai Village. The police said other members of the criminal gang escaped with suspected gunshot injuries. Items recovered during the operation included an unregistered Haojue motorcycle, ₦308,000 in cash, a chain and a jerrycan. The command said it had intensified security patrols and surveillance in the area, adding that efforts were ongoing to track down the fleeing suspects and bring all those involved to justice. The Commissioner of Police, CP Umar M. Hadejia, commended the operatives and their local vigilante collaborators for their prompt response, courage and effective coordination. He reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property, disrupting criminal networks and ensuring that perpetrators of violent crimes were brought to justice. Hadejia also urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to strengthen collective security efforts. nigeria.title: 2027: Makinde backs state police, vows security overhaul
nigeria.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has backed the establishment of state police, pledging to decentralise Nigeria’s security architecture if elected president in the 2027 general elections. Makinde stated this on Sunday during a live political programme on Jay FM 101.9 in Jos, Plateau State, where he outlined his proposed security reforms ahead of the party’s presidential campaign activities in the city. “I believe that we need to decentralise our security architecture. State police is one of the ways to achieve this, but it must be properly structured. “States that are ready should be allowed to establish their own police formations, while others can come on board when they are prepared,” he said. Recalling his engagement with former President Muhammadu Buhari on the issue in 2019, Makinde said the former president had expressed concerns about the ability of some states to fund their police formations. “When we approached President Buhari in 2019, one of the concerns he raised was that some states could not even pay workers’ salaries. He questioned how such states would be able to fund state police,” he said. Explaining the alternative adopted by governors in the South-West, Makinde said they settled for a regional security arrangement through Amotekun. He said the operatives gather intelligence and work with federal security agencies, adding that the initiative had helped improve security coordination in the region. The APM presidential candidate acknowledged concerns that state police could be abused by governors to intimidate political opponents and other citizens, but insisted that appropriate safeguards could address such risks. “We must not pretend that there are no concerns. Some people are worried that governors could use state police to oppress their opponents or intimidate citizens. Those concerns are valid, and we must put safeguards in place. “But the fact that something can be abused does not mean we should not do it. We must design a system that ensures accountability and protects the rights of the people,” he said. On the pace of implementation, Makinde said states should be allowed to establish their police formations at different times, depending on their readiness and capacity. He cited Nigeria’s transition to self-government and independence as an example of how states could adopt the arrangement at different paces. “We had self-government in 1957 and independence in 1960. nigeria.title: Lagos 2027: PDP’s Deji Doherty Defends Alliance With Wike, Tinubu
nigeria.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Lagos State, Adedeji Doherty, has defended his political relationship with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, despite the latter’s support for President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC). Doherty said Wike’s position in the APC-led Federal Government does not make him an enemy of democracy, arguing that politics and democracy can accommodate different political alignments. He spoke during the 2027 Lagos State governorship debate organised by Channels Television, TVC, Punch Newspapers, Vanguard Newspapers and The Cable on Sunday. Responding to a question on how he could offer a genuine opposition alternative in Lagos despite emerging from a PDP faction loyal to Wike, Doherty said his candidacy was the product of 26 years of political work and grassroots support. “My emergence in the People’s Democratic Party is out of 26 years of hard work, consistency, determination, and continued support for the grassroots. I have built a grassroots structure right from scratch, and I know there are a lot of people here that can testify to that. That’s number one. “Number two is that Nyesom Wike is our leader. He’s our national leader. He will continue to be my leader, and he will continue to show us that politics and democracy are not enemies,” he said. The PDP candidate further defended Wike’s relationship with the President, pointing to what he described as benefits from the Federal Government. “Once we are getting results from the FCT, we are getting results from Mr. President, we are getting monies into the pockets of governors in different states,” Doherty added. business.title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Inside the Story of Martell’s Afrobeats Limited Edition XO with Davido and Prince Gyasi
entertainment.description: There’s something special about a collaboration that brings together music and visual art, particularly when both creatives have spent years helping African culture reach audiences around the world. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. Reimagined through Gyasi’s distinctive, hyper-surreal visual style, these elements create a composition that captures the movement and energy of Afrobeats while celebrating the unity, strength and creative spirit of the continent. For Gyasi, the inspiration goes beyond the visual appeal of the bottle. Growing up in Ghana, his experience of music and its ability to bring people together informed the creative direction of the collaboration. “Growing up in Ghana, I’ve seen firsthand how music brings people together, sparking connection, celebration, and pure joy. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. entertainment.title: UK-based OBIMI Brings Families Together in Lagos to Support Children With Disabilities
entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. sports.title: Best division ever? How NFC North is on pace to make history in 2026

The Bears found a way to win on Sunday night, overcoming five turnovers to defeat the Buccaneers 27-24, but they certainly aren't alone in the NFC North. The Packers and Lions both continued their winning ways on Sunday, and, until Monday at least, none of those three teams can say they only one loss like the Vikings do. All four NFC North teams will enter Week 10 in the playoff picture. While head-to-head matchups might hurt the division's chances of getting every team into the playoffs, it's becoming clear these four teams are in a class of their own as a group. Here's a look at how the NFC North could be headed for uncharted territory. MORE: Which NFL trade candidates boosted - or hurt - their stocks in Week 9? NFC North combined record The NFC North is now 25-8 (.757) through nearly nine weeks, with five of those eight losses simply coming against one another. NFC North teams are 20-3 in non-divisional games. Here are the standings after Sunday night, with the Vikings still to play on Monday: Team Record Pct. Vikings 6-1 .857 Bears 7-2 .778 Lions 6-2 .750 Packers 6-3 .667 Every team in the division is at least three games over .500, meaning the Packers are in last place at 6-3. In the NFC North, for comparison, the 3-5 Panthers lead the division. The Bears have had a hard time gaining ground during the four-game win streak because of all of the success around them, but a Vikings loss to the Bills on Monday night would rocket Chicago into first place. MORE: 4 quarterbacks who boosted their early MVP cases in Week 9 Best division in NFL history When it comes to divisions, there are two distinct periods in the NFL: pre-2002, when divisions were larger than four teams, and 2002-present, when all divisions have been comprised of four teams. The overall records within divisions were more even before 2002 because more teams were in each. Since 2002, the best record for a division belongs to the 2024 NFC North, which saw teams go a combined 45-23 (.662) as the Lions went 15-2, Vikings went 14-3, Packers went 11-6 and Bears went 7-10. Two years earlier, in the NFC East went a combined 43-23-2, sending three teams to the playoffs. So far, the NFC North is on track to break its own record in 2026. At 25-8 (.757), every team is at least three games above .500 and their combined record would have to be 20-15 the rest of the way to match the 2024 mark. There are still seven divisional games on the docket in the NFC North, so the division will have at least 15 losses. If these four teams can keep it to only eight additional losses, the division will tie its own record from 2002. sports.title: Mitch Albom: Lions won't have many easy wins. But does it matter?
sports.description: Dan Campbell knew what this was by halftime. He barked it into the CBS cameras. “We gotta calm down … and then we GOTTA GO! We can’t be messing around!” Exactly. When playing a team that is 1-6, a good team often finds itself inexplicably fumbling and bumbling. It’s like when you can’t get that first piece of plastic to peel off the box. You start normal, then you try your fingernails, then you get frustrated, and you wind up screaming to yourself, “Why is this so damn hard?” That was the Detroit Lions for much of Sunday’s game in Miami against the low-win but high-effort Dolphins . Detroit’s first drive used up nearly seven minutes but ended with a sack of Jared Goff on third-and-goal. A field goal had to suffice. Their second drive ended in an interception, when Goff was pressured and a defender hit his arm as he tried to pass. Their third drive ended with a punt. Their fourth drive, after starting with great field position, fizzled when Jahmyr Gibbs was yanked down twice in a row for thre- yard losses and Goff was pressured into a scramble. Another field goal. The NFL’s highest-flying offense was hovering very close to the ground. Fortunately, Miami couldn’t take advantage. They punted twice, notched a field goal, and wasted an 11-play drive with a doink off the uprights by their kicker, Zane Gonzalez. Halftime ended at Lions 6, Miami 3. Which is what led Campbell to his “we can’t be messing around” critique, which I’m sure he delivered in the locker room with a fervor that would have scared the average TV viewer. And eventually, they did stop messing around. And they finally brought home a 19-9 win that may have certain critics attacking them for, well, not being able to get the plastic off a box faster than that. They’d be wrong. It swirled around practice all week. When one football player sees another football player face down and not moving, it stays with them − believe me. Four plays into the second half, safety Chuck Clark snagged a Malik Willis pass and turned into a running back, cutting angles and using blocks. He returned the ball 34 yards to the Miami 26. sports.title: Boston Celtics rally to stomp Milwaukee Bucks, 117-97, and improve to 8-2
sports.description: Effort is difficult to quantify in the NBA. However, there are a few areas of the game that can occasionally reveal its presence. For an example of this phenomenon during the Boston Celtics' 117-97 win over the Milwaukee Bucks on Sunday night, look no further than the final offensive rebound totals. The C's corralled a whopping 20 offensive boards at Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee while the Bucks only grabbed 9. Such a significant disparity suggests that the Celtics, who trailed 20-6 about halfway through the first quarter, stepped up their effort when things didn't immediately go their way. In fact, 4 of Boston's 6 offensive rebounds in the first frame occurred after it went down double digits. Meanwhile, Milwaukee had 0 offensive rebounds in that same span, and just 1 in the entire first quarter. Because the Celtics dominated the glass, they ended up with 16 more field goal attempts than the Bucks. From there, it's a math game, as Boston converted on 45 of its 95 shots (47.4 percent from the field) while Milwaukee hit 35 of its 79 shots (44.3 percent from the field). As for the rest of the margins, the Celtics garnered 12 steals — another effort-related stat — to the Bucks' 5 and prevailed in the points in the paint battle, 44-28. All of these numbers added up to the Celtics' third straight win and the Bucks' sixth straight loss. Before the now 8-2 Celtics face the 9-2 Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday night in a highly-anticipated matchup, let's take a closer look at the most memorable moments from Boston's blowout victory captured in images below. sports.description: Credit: Dennis Lee-Imagn Images Kings crowd left in stunned silence after scary Keegan Murray fall vs. Heat appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Sunday night, Keegan Murray made his return for the Sacramento Kings in a tussle against the Miami Heat after a seven-game absence due to a left ankle injury. The Kings brought him back slowly, as Murray came off the bench behind De’Andre Hunter and didn’t check into the game until over four minutes had passed in the first quarter. It did not take long until Murray found himself near peril once more. With less than two minutes remaining in the first quarter, the recently-returned Kings forward leapt high near the rim before Heat big man Bobby Portis even attempted a shot. Murray then suffered a hard fall as Portis went underneath him, undercutting him and sending him crashing to the ground with a scary fall. The good news is that Murray was able to brace for impact, preventing him from landing on his head. Moreover, in a testament to his athleticism, he was able to roll a bit to his side to dampen the force of the blow he would take from landing on the hardwood. The Kings would immediately sub him out after this play. The 26-year-old forward has already gone through quite a few injury problems over the past few seasons. He played in just 23 games last season after ankle injuries plagued him all season long, and he already had to miss time earlier this year due to similar ankle issues. science.title: Legendary sci-fi magazine 'Starlog' returns as a yearly release, just in time for its 50th anniversary
science.description: null "Starlog" was one of the greatest sci-fi and fantasy magazines ever, and after a 17-year absence, it's being resurrected. The legendary sci-fi mag went dark back in 2009 as part of the wave of popular publications folding due to years of declining readership and subscriptions. But as of Nov. 13, this geek favorite periodical returns as an annual print edition, and it's available for pre-order now. It’s another indication of digital fatigue in the world, and fans of a certain age will recall the pleasure of poring over each colorful issue packed with in-depth interviews, behind-the-scenes photos, TV guides, classic movie retrospectives, book reviews, con news, and VFX features. The triumphant relaunch of "Starlog" magazine happens on Nov. 13, 2026 (Image credit: Fangoria Holdings) "Starlog" launched in 1976, in the pre-" Star Wars " days, under the leadership of editor-in-chief Kerry O’Quinn. It first arrived with artist Jack Thurston's beautiful painted "Star Trek" cover, featuring William Shatner as Captain James T. Kirk and Leonard Nimoy’s Spock, set against the U.S.S. Enterprise near a shimmering black hole. The magazine continued to inform the science fiction community about upcoming sci-fi TV shows and blockbuster Hollywood films for over three decades; I fondly recall reading each informative and entertaining monthly issue cover-to-cover. Just in time to honor its 50th anniversary this year, "Starlog" blasts back into the sci-fi universe with Issue #375 showcasing cover artwork created by Armenian artist Gabriel Yeganyan. Its geek culture legacy, covering iconic franchises like "Star Wars," "Star Trek," and "Alien," will now live on thanks to Fangoria Holdings and io9 co-founder Annalee Newitz, editor-in-chief. Three vintage "Starlog" magazine issues from my personal collection! (Image credit: Jeff Spry) "During its original 33-year run, 'Starlog' documented science fiction as it evolved across film, television, books, technology, and culture," said 'Fangoria's Tara Ansley. "Fifty years after the magazine first launched, the line between science fiction and the real world has become increasingly difficult to separate. That makes this an especially interesting time to bring 'Starlog' back. Technology may change, but the most compelling questions have always been about people: how we live, what we create, and what kind of future we want to build." "Starlog" reloads for its first annual edition after a long hiatus on Nov. 13. You can pre-order the first issue (Issue 375 in continuity) on the Starlog website .

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
science.description: null On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this. It performed well, but eventually it stopped listening to commands. The spacecraft burned up in the atmosphere in January 2015. A Russian Soyuz rocket launches the Venus Express spacecraft to Venus on Nov. 8, 2005.. (Image credit: ESA) Why it mattered Venus Express established ESA as the third world organization to successfully send a probe to study Venus, following the United States and Soviet Union. (Japan's JAXA became the fourth five years later.) "By studying Venus, scientists learn how Earth-like planets change over time," reads a summary of the planet's exploration prepared by The Planetary Society. "Orbital studies [like Venus Express] hint that Venus may have hosted habitable oceans before becoming inhospitable." "By studying Venus, we can learn how Earth-like planets evolve and what shapes planets throughout the galaxy into temperate, lush worlds instead of sweltering hothouses. Venus also helps scientists model Earth’s climate, and may serve as a cautionary tale on how dramatically a planet’s climate can change," wrote the Society. An illustration of the Venus Express spacecraft in orbit around Venus. (Image credit: ESA) ESA returned to Venus in 2018 when BepiColombo, its joint mission with JAXA, used the planet's gravity to redirect its path toward the planet Mercury. Want more space history? science.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
science.description: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life. To aid in distinguishing between habitable and inhabited planets, planetary scientist Samantha Gilbert-Janizek of the University of California, Riverside, developed a model that simulates the evolution of a rocky planet without life. "The model can help us see how habitable but non-living planets might mimic living planets," Gilbert-Janizek, who was a PhD student at the University of Washington when the research was conducted, said in a statement. Gilbert-Janizek built upon a model previously developed by Washington’s Rory Barnes that simulated the core, mantle, and crust of a planet. This new model pushed the simulation two steps further by incorporating the surface and atmosphere of the planet as well. In all, the model simulates 19 properties of a rocky planet that are not related to life, including the amount of heat a planet receives from its star , the exchange of heat and chemicals from the core to the surface, and the outflow of certain gases from the subsurface. Gilbert-Janizek’s starting point was to simulate the development of Earth had life never arisen here, therefore providing a baseline with which to compare to exoplanets . She ran the simulation from the birth of Earth 4.5 billion years ago to 500 million years into the future. The result was a lifeless world, but one that still had oceans and an atmosphere. "When we interpret observations of an exoplanet’s atmosphere, this tool will help us determine the probability that what we observe indicates life on the surface," said Gilbert-Janizek. An illustration shows the landscape of a primordial Earth before life arose as lightning splits the skies (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) What makes the simulation especially useful is its plug-and-play nature. Researchers can simply apply the bulk properties of whichever planet they are studying to the model, and then just let it run. If the result is a planet with an atmosphere that matches what is detected spectroscopically by the James Webb Space Telescope or, in the future, the various extremely large 30-meter-plus ground-based telescopes or NASA’s planned Habitable Worlds Observatory , then we know that planet probably does not have life as we know it. Credit: NASA NASA announced a suite of awards and mission updates on Saturday to expand the agency’s Moon Base exploration, science, and infrastructure capabilities. The investments will advance commercial robotic deliveries, a nuclear-powered rover named PROMISE, launch and orbital transfer services, and surface infrastructure as the agency works with American industry to establish a sustained presence on the Moon’s South Pole. The agency shared the news at the MAX POWER aerospace expo and air show at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. “We are building the Moon Base mission by mission,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “Today’s announcements expand nearly every part of that campaign, using the playbook that carried NASA through its greatest eras: fly often, learn, apply those lessons, and get more better and more capable with every mission. When our astronauts return to the Moon, they will arrive with the first elements of the Moon Base already waiting for them on the surface.” “In the eight months since Ignition, we’ve made incredible strides in accomplishing the near impossible: establishing a permanent outpost on the lunar surface,” said Carlos García-Galán, manager, Moon Base Program. “We’ve consolidated numerous efforts into a streamlined program, evolving our human exploration architecture into an iterative and sustained campaign for Moon Base technology development and implementation. Most importantly, we’ve taken action, awarding new contracts and forging new partnerships to accelerate development.” Moon Base cargo landers To strengthen the cargo lander network needed to support the Moon Base, NASA selected eight companies for the next phase of its CLPS ( Commercial Lunar Payload Services ) initiative. The companies are eligible to compete for future lunar surface delivery missions under the new CLPS 2 contract: Blue Origin Firefly Aerospace Intuitive Machines ispace-U.S. Lockheed Martin Space Northrop Grumman Space Systems SpaceX Voyager Technologies Under the CLPS 2 framework, the companies will provide lunar delivery services, including managing, building, and operating landers that transport NASA science, technology, and infrastructure payloads to the Moon. The CLPS 2 framework is a 10-year, multiple-award, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity master contract with a combined maximum value of $10 billion. science.title: NASA Seeks Next Generation of Explorers to Join Astronaut Corps
science.description: NASA announced its 2025 Astronaut Candidate Class on Sept. 22, 2025, at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Credit: NASA/Helen Arase Vargas NASA is looking for the explorers who will help write the next chapter of human spaceflight. Applications are now open for the agency’s next class of astronauts, who will join NASA as America returns to the Moon, builds the Moon Base, and lays the groundwork for the first crewed missions to Mars. The next generation of astronauts will train to operate on the lunar surface, live and work beyond Earth, and take on missions that will push the boundaries of human exploration farther than ever before. U.S. citizens interested in joining the astronaut corps have until 11:59 p.m. EST Thursday, Dec. 3, to submit their completed application materials at: https://go.nasa.gov/3WyvlQi “This is an extraordinary time to join NASA’s astronaut corps,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “The people we select could walk on the Moon, live and work at the Moon Base, and help pioneer the systems and operations that will ultimately carry crews to Mars. Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage. NASA’s astronaut corps has always called on remarkable Americans willing to take on extraordinary challenges in service to the nation. If you are ready to join that tradition, come help write the next chapter of humanity’s greatest adventure.” NASA expects to make its final selection in late 2027 to begin training as the next class of astronaut candidates. “The window is open. The mission is waiting. And the only thing missing from the greatest adventure humanity has ever embarked upon is you,” said NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson. The agency last opened applications in 2024. From more than 8,000 applications, 10 astronaut candidates were selected in 2025 and are currently completing nearly two years of training. “For those who apply, becoming a NASA astronaut is more than a career opportunity,” said Scott Tingle, chief astronaut and chair of the Astronaut Selection Board at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. “It is a chance to join a legacy of explorers who have pushed the boundaries of discovery and play a role in the missions that will shape humanity’s future in space. The next generation of astronaut candidates could help write history while inspiring future scientists, engineers, and explorers.” Since the 1960s, NASA has selected 370 people to train as astronaut candidates for its increasingly challenging missions. The agency has 32 astronauts active in the astronaut corps, and selected applicants will join their ranks to study spacewalking, lunar geology, operations of high-performance aircraft, and more. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history?
